issue.title: sase-core memory_history spawns ~9 git processes per warm query (upstream count, repo identity, index/tree probes), missing the 30ms fresh-check budget
issue.description: Proposed fix: memoize repo identity (toplevel, git-common-dir, object format) per scope key; compute upstream_ahead only during an explicit sync or refresh, never on every query; batch the per-path ls-files and ls-tree probes; and read HEAD without spawning git when that is cheap. Then re-measure the plan's section 5.5 index budgets (cold <= 1.5s, incremental over 100 commits <= 100ms, warm fresh <= 30ms) and update the Performance section of docs/memory_history.md with the measured numbers. A sase repo pin ratchet (sase-core-revision.txt) is needed only if Python starts depending on new behavior.

task_type_fields.location: crates/sase_core/src/memory_history/cache.rs (sync_scope freshness probe) and query.rs/upstream.rs in sase-core
task_type_fields.repro:
Measured on the sase repo on 2026-10-01 at f28d171585, with a warm snapshot and the sase-core binding from pin 6a341a9:

    from sase.memory.history.service import HistoryService
    s = HistoryService(); sc = s.project_scope(Path('.').resolve())
    s.timeline(sc, 'sase/memory/gotchas.md')   # warm it
    # then time repeated calls with GIT_TRACE=<file>

- Each warm query is slow: sync p50 45.7ms / p95 54.6ms, timeline p50 75-89ms, version (with body) p50 57.7ms. The budget in plan:202609/memory_history.md section 5.5 is a 30ms warm fresh check.
- GIT_TRACE shows 9 git processes for one warm timeline() call: rev-parse --git-common-dir, rev-parse HEAD, symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, rev-list --first-parent --count HEAD..origin/master -- <instruction paths>, rev-parse --show-toplevel, ls-files -s -z -- <path>, rev-parse --show-object-format, ls-tree -z HEAD -- <path>, and one more.
- The snapshot itself is already memoized in-process (cache.rs snapshot_memo), so the per-call cost is the probes.
- Launch phase sase-1dr.12 (note #8) also measured a cold index build of 2.3s against a 1.5s budget; sase-1dr.5 (notes #1 and #3) measured 6.5s cold before the runner fix.

issue.creation_reason: Filed by the sase-1dr land agent from sase-1dr.5 note #3 and sase-1dr.12 note #8, after reproducing the warm-query miss and tracing its root cause; the Python CLI import overhead from the same notes is being fixed as epic work.
